statement.p: Find the gradient of the function f(x,y,z) = z^{2}\ln\mathopen{}\left(yx\right), at the point (e,1,-1)

static.solution: f_x=z^{2}\frac{1}{yx}y, f_y=z^{2}\frac{1}{yx}x and f_z =2z\ln\mathopen{}\left(yx\right). Thus \mbox{grad} f = \frac{z^{2}\cdot 1}{yx}y\,\mathit{\vec i}+\frac{z^{2}\cdot 1}{yx}x\,\mathit{\vec j}+2z\ln\mathopen{}\left(yx\right)\,\mathit{\vec k} and \nabla f(e,1,-1) = 0.367879\,\mathit{\vec i}+\,\mathit{\vec j}-2\,\mathit{\vec k}.
